droppedAngles.title: silent-drops
droppedAngles.why: No field is renamed, added, or moved across a store/serialisation boundary. ownerId and actorId are already in store.js's SCHEMA for 'accounts' and 'audit' respectively, written and read back under the same names before and after this diff; openAccount still builds its store.insert() object as an explicit literal (not a spread of the options), so no stray key from the caller's object was ever stored, before or after.

droppedAngles.title: security
droppedAngles.why: No new injection, secret, redirect, or CORS surface. The one touched route now passes an explicit {label, currency} object instead of spreading req.body, which narrows rather than widens what a client can influence, and openAccount never spreads its options into the stored row.

droppedAngles.title: data-integrity
droppedAngles.why: Nothing here touches concurrency, caching, retries, or partial writes -- it's a synchronous call-signature rewrite over the existing single-process Store.insert/update calls, which are unchanged by this diff.

droppedAngles.title: migrations-and-rollout
droppedAngles.why: No schema or data migration, and the app is a single deployable process with no client/server version-skew window for a function signature -- every src/ and test/ call site is updated in the same commit. (A missed non-test caller does exist, but that's a boundary-contract question, not a rollout/migration one.)

scoutNotes: openAccount's signature changes from a single options object (ownerId, label, currency, actorId all equal) to (store, actor, {label, currency, ownerId = actor.id}), so the audit record now derives from actor.id and ownerId defaults to the actor but can diverge. The diff updates openAccount's one production caller (the POST /accounts route in src/server.js, which now forwards only {label, currency} instead of spreading req.body) and every call site in test/accounts.test.js and test/transfers.test.js to the new positional shape.

confirmed.title: seed.mjs still calls openAccount with the old options-object shape
confirmed.rootCause: scripts/seed.mjs was never updated for openAccount's new (store, actor, options) signature and still calls it with the old single options-object shape, so that object binds to the new `actor` parameter, the third `options` parameter is left undefined, and the call throws on destructuring undefined before actor.id is ever evaluated.
confirmed.summary: The diff changes openAccount's signature to (store, actor, options) but scripts/seed.mjs, a caller left untouched by the diff, still calls it with the pre-refactor two-argument shape openAccount(store, { ownerId, label, actorId }), so the new second parameter `actor` binds to that plain options object instead of a user, the third parameter is left undefined, and the function throws before it even reaches the ownerId/actor.id logic.
confirmed.failure: Running `node scripts/seed.mjs` (as README.md's quick-start documents) throws `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'label' of 'undefined' as it is undefined` at src/accounts.js:9 from the call at scripts/seed.mjs:26, because the old-shape options object binds to the new `actor` parameter and the third `options` argument is undefined; the script exits non-zero with no users or accounts seeded.

confirmed.reasoning: Confirmed directly. scripts/seed.mjs is not touched by this PR's diff (the diff only modifies src/accounts.js, src/server.js, test/accounts.test.js, test/transfers.test.js) and still calls openAccount(store, { ownerId: member.id, label: 'Everyday', actorId: member.id }) — the old single-options-object shape. The new signature is openAccount(store, actor, { label, currency = 'AUD', ownerId = actor.id }). Running `LEDGER_FILE=/tmp/seed-test-ledger.json node scripts/seed.mjs` in the checked-out worktree reproduced exactly the claimed crash: `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'label' of 'undefined' as it is undefined` thrown at src/accounts.js:9 from the call at scripts/seed.mjs:26, exit code 1. Verified README.md line 9 documents `node scripts/seed.mjs` as the quick-start seed command, matching the claim's framing. This is a real regression introduced by this diff: it changed openAccount's signature but left one of its callers (seed.mjs) on the old call shape, breaking the documented seed workflow before any users/accounts are created.
confirmed.panel: 3 of 3 skeptics could not refute it

missed.what: src/server.js's POST /accounts handler changed from `openAccount(store, { ...body, ownerId: user.id, actorId: user.id })` to `openAccount(store, user, { label: body.label, currency: body.currency })`. Spreading `null` in JS is safe (`{...null}` === `{}`), so a request whose JSON body is the literal `null` previously fell through to the existing 'label is required' 400 validation. The new code dereferences `body.label` directly, which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'label')` on a null body -- caught by the server's generic handler and surfaced as a 500 'internal error' (with a server-side console.error) instead of the prior clean 400. Verified empirically by POSTing a literal `null` body to a running server built from this diff: got `500 {"error":"internal error"}` where the pre-diff code path would have produced `400 {"error":"label is required"}`. This directly contradicts the PR's 'no behaviour change' claim and is not covered by any existing test (no test in test/*.js sends a null body).
missed.why: boundary-contract and silent-drops were scoped to the store/serialisation boundary (field renames across SCHEMA), not the HTTP request-body boundary -- this bug lives entirely in how the route dereferences `body`, with no field renamed or dropped in storage. security was scoped to injection/widening of what a client can influence in the stored row; this is a narrowing of accepted fields that happens to remove a prior null-safety side effect, which isn't a security-widening concern. tests-that-dont-test and correctness looked at whether the refactored call sites preserve the SAME assertions as before, not at untested HTTP edge-case inputs the diff newly makes reachable. data-integrity and migrations-and-rollout were scoped to concurrency/versioning, irrelevant here. So no angle was positioned to catch an edge case that only appears when you trace what `body.label` evaluates to for every possible parsed-JSON shape, including the one value (`null`) where property access and object-spread diverge.
